claims.object_text: part of the GATOR1 complex that inhibits mTORC1
claims.quote: DEP-domain containing-5 (DEPDC5) is part of the GATOR1 complex that inhibits the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex-1 (mTORC1).
Loss-of-function mutations in human DEPDC5 are the most common cause of lesional or non-lesional focal epilepsies associated with mTOR hyperactivation.

claims.object_text: Depdc5 silencing leads to excitation/inhibition imbalance and increased excitatory synapse strength
claims.quote: Depdc5 silencing in mature neurons leads to excitation/inhibition imbalance and increased excitatory synapse strength.

claims.object_text: conditional knockout (cKO) mouse recapitulates excitatory/inhibitory imbalance with increased excitatory transmission and unaffected inhibitory transmission
claims.quote: genetic deletion of Depdc5 in a conditional knockout (cKO) mouse recapitulates the excitatory/inhibitory imbalance observed after transient Depdc5 silencing, with increased strength of excitatory transmission and unaffected inhibitory transmission.

claims.object_text: higher density of GluA1-containing AMPA receptors due to shift of GluA1 from intracellular pool to plasma membrane
claims.quote: the increased glutamate quantal size and response to exogenous glutamate are attributable to a higher density of GluA1-containing AMPA glutamate receptors due to a shift of the GluA1 subunit from the intracellular pool to the plasma membrane.

claims.object_text: interacts with WDR48, WDR20, and USP46
claims.quote: The DEPDC5 protein interaction network included WDR48, WDR20, and USP46, a ubiquitin-specific protease that regulates GluA1, as key binding partners

claims.object_text: absence of DEPDC5 increases USP46 levels and decreases ubiquitination of GluA1
claims.quote: In the absence of DEPDC5, USP46 levels increase, and ubiquitination of GluA1 decreases accordingly.

claims.object_text: knockdown of USP46 or rapamycin treatment rescues increased glutamate quantal size and USP46 increase caused by Depdc5 deletion
claims.quote: Either knockdown of USP46 or rapamycin treatment rescues both the increased glutamate quantal size and USP46 increase caused by Depdc5 deletion

claims.object_text: USP46 overexpression depends on mTORC1 hyperactivity
claims.quote: indicating that USP46 overexpression depends on mTORC1 hyperactivity.

claims.object_text: DEPDC5/mTORC1 system controls excitatory strength by negatively modulating USP46 activity and AMPA receptor deubiquitination
claims.quote: the DEPDC5/mTORC1 system physiologically controls the excitatory strength by negatively modulating USP46 activity and AMPA receptor deubiquitination
failure of this effect can contribute to the development of the Depdc5-linked epileptic phenotype.
